subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept this custom yielding glob walker and bootstrap-only hook scheduling as the bounded fix for bootstrap-context event-loop stalls?
rationale: The implementation is focused and well-proven, but bootstrap file selection, prompt bytes, and hook timing are upgrade-sensitive session surfaces whose tradeoff requires owner intent.

options.title: Land after exact-head verification
options.body: Accept the internal mitigation after rebase and exact-head parity, SDK-surface, type, and focused runtime validation.

options.title: Require connected runtime proof
options.body: Keep the implementation but require one current-head embedded-run or channel-latency transcript before accepting the scheduling change.

options.title: Pause for broader architecture
options.body: Hold the PR if maintainers prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or caching rather than maintaining a custom walker.

recommendation.title: Land after exact-head verification
recommendation.body: Accept the internal mitigation after rebase and exact-head parity, SDK-surface, type, and focused runtime validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history spans all three compatibility-sensitive surfaces: guarded workspace reads, bootstrap hooks, and internal dispatch.
